APPLICATION FOR PROTECTION ORDER: FORM 6 AND FORM 6A
Domestic Violence Act, 1998 (Act No. 116 of 1998), section 4(1). Domestic Violence Regulations 2022 (published 14 April 2023), Form 6 [Regulation 7(1)] and Form 6A [Regulation 7(1A)]. Court form J480, updated 7 March 2025.

This replaces the older "Form 2" from the 1999 regulations, which were repealed. The application is made by affidavit. It can be handed to the clerk of the court in person, sent electronically, or submitted through the online portal.

Form 6 is the application itself. Form 6A holds the complainant's personal information. Form 6A is for office use and is NOT served on the respondent, so the complainant's address, contact details and the details of children and witnesses are kept away from the respondent.

FORM 6: APPLICATION FOR PROTECTION ORDER
PART A: APPLICATION

1. PARTICULARS OF COMPLAINANT (Victim of domestic violence)
- Surname
- Full names

2. PARTICULARS OF PERSON MAKING THE APPLICATION ON BEHALF OF THE COMPLAINANT (if applicable)
- Surname; Full names
- Capacity: Care giver; Counsellor; Educator; Family member; Health care personnel; Medical practitioner; Official in public health establishment; Related person (having a close relationship with the complainant); Social worker; South African Police Service member; Other (specify)

3. PARTICULARS OF PERSON WHO COMMITTED ACT OF DOMESTIC VIOLENCE (hereafter called the Respondent)
- Relationship to the complainant (tick): for example boyfriend, girlfriend, ex-boyfriend, ex-girlfriend, current co-resident, ex-co-resident in the past year, husband, wife, ex-husband, ex-wife, ex-partner, intimate or sexual partner of any duration, partner, partner in a perceived relationship, partner in an alleged marriage; brother, sister, daughter, son, father, mother, parent of child/children; in-laws and ex-in-laws; step-relatives; aunt, uncle, cousin, nephew, niece; other (specify)
- Surname (if known)
- Full names or name known to you by
- ID number / date of birth if known, or estimated age
- Home address (if known)
- Home/work/other contact telephone number (if known); Cell phone number (if known)
- Email address (if known)
- Social media platform(s) on which the respondent has accounts (if known), and the respondent's name, handle or number on each account (if known)
- Work/school/study address (if known)
- Occupation, including learner/student (if known)

4. INFORMATION REGARDING ACTS OF DOMESTIC VIOLENCE
- History of abuse. Documents, photos, witness statements and medical records can be attached.
- Most recent incident: Date; Place where it happened (or social media account details if it happened online); Details of what happened; Any injuries (including what was used); Any medical, psychological or other treatment received; Harm or damages caused
- The same questions again for another incident
- Other information the court should know

5. INFORMATION REGARDING URGENCY OF APPLICATION
- Why is the application urgent?
- Any other reasons why you need to get a protection order today?
- Are you still staying in the same place as the respondent?
- Are there firearms or other weapons in the house? Give details
- Does the respondent carry or have access to a firearm for work purposes or activities? Give details
- Do you fear for your life or safety, or the safety of your children, other relatives or people you know? Give details
- Does the respondent use drugs, so that a referral to a treatment centre for substance abuse is needed? Give details

6. TERMS OF PROTECTION ORDER
It is requested that the respondent must be ordered (mark the appropriate box and complete where necessary):
(a) Not to commit or attempt to commit the following acts towards the complainant: Physical abuse; Sexual abuse; Emotional, verbal or psychological abuse; Economic abuse; Intimidation; Harassment; Sexual harassment; Related person abuse; Spiritual abuse; Damage to property; Elder abuse; Coercive behaviour; Abusive behaviour; Degrading behaviour; Controlling behaviour; Exposure of a child to domestic violence; Intimidating behaviour; Threatening behaviour; Offensive behaviour; Humiliating behaviour
(b) Not to get the help of another person to commit any act in (a)
(c) Not to enter the shared residence, situated at: [address]
(d) Not to enter a specified part of the shared residence, namely: [part]
(e) Not to enter the complainant's residence, situated at: [address]
(f) Not to enter the complainant's workplace or place of studies, namely: [details]
(g) Not to prevent the complainant or any child who ordinarily lives or lived in the shared residence from entering or remaining in the shared residence or any part of it
(h) Not to disclose or make available any electronic communication, especially the following: [details]
(i) Not to commit any other act, namely: [details]

7. ADDITIONAL CONDITIONS
It is also requested that the court must order that (complete where necessary):
(a) A peace officer, namely [name], accompanies the complainant to collect personal property (see paragraph 8)
(b) A member of the South African Police Service seizes the following weapon(s) in the possession of the respondent
(c) The respondent pays interim rent or mortgage payments until the return date
(d) The respondent pays interim maintenance until the return date
(e) The respondent pays interim emergency monetary relief until the return date, for example food, necessities, transport, medical, dental, medication, counselling, school fees, relocation costs and household bills
(f) The respondent is refused any contact with the following child or children until the return date
(g) The respondent is granted the following contact with the following child or children until the return date
(h) The complainant's home, study or work details must not be disclosed to the respondent: Yes / No
(i) Other conditions requested

8. PERSONAL PROPERTY
Property description; Grounds on which the property is considered to be personal property; Address where the property is kept. Furniture such as beds and lounge suites is not personal property.

9. I am likely to report a breach of the protection order at the [name] Police Station.

10. The court I will be able to attend is [name].

11. INDEX OF ANNEXURES TO THIS FORM (documents attached, each marked with a letter and a short description)

Signature of complainant or person applying on behalf of the complainant; Date

PART B: CERTIFICATE (completed by the Commissioner of Oaths or Justice of the Peace when the affidavit is sworn or affirmed)

FORM 6A: PERSONAL INFORMATION FOR OFFICE USE AND NOT FOR SERVICE ON RESPONDENT

1. PARTICULARS OF COMPLAINANT (Victim of domestic violence)
- Surname; Full names; ID number / date of birth; Gender; Race; Type of disability (if any); Marital status
- Home or temporary address; Home/contact telephone number; Cell phone number for application updates; Email address
- Would you prefer to have the matter heard through an audiovisual link (if available)? Email address or contact number for the audiovisual link; any other social media account where the court can contact you
- Work address; Work telephone number
- Nature of domestic relationship with the respondent
- Occupation (including learner/student)

2. PARTICULARS OF PERSON MAKING THE APPLICATION ON BEHALF OF THE VICTIM (if applicable)
- Surname; Full names; ID number / date of birth; Gender; Race; Type of disability (if any); Marital status; Email address; Work address; Work telephone number; Occupation
- Reason(s) why the application is made on behalf of the victim
- Whether written consent of the victim has been obtained and is attached, or why consent is not necessary (the victim is a child who cannot apply, a person with a mental disability, unconscious, or unable to consent for another stated reason)

3. PERSONS AFFECTED BY DOMESTIC VIOLENCE
3.1 Particulars of children and adults sharing the residence: Name; Age; Relationship to complainant
3.2 How are these persons affected?
3.3 Do any of these persons have disabilities? If so, give details
- Name and contact details of any person who witnessed the incident

KEY NOTES FOR COMPLETING THE FORM
- Section 4 (acts of domestic violence) is the most important part: give the most recent incident in full, then another incident, then the history and how it has escalated.
- Section 5 (urgency) supports an interim order: explain why the court must act now.
- The terms requested in Section 6 must match the abuse described in Section 4.
- Section 7 conditions should support the safety needs described.
- Section 2 and Form 6A section 2 are only completed if someone else is applying on the complainant's behalf.
- Personal details that could help the respondent find the complainant belong on Form 6A, which is not served on the respondent.
